# The running example

## The Dow Jones 30

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: download-dj30-r
#| cache: true
symbols <- download_data(
  domain = "Index Constituents",
  index = "Dow Jones Industrial Average"
)

prices_daily <- download_data(
  domain = "Stock Prices",
  symbols = symbols$symbol,
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: download-dj30-py
#| eval: false
symbols = tf.download_data(
    domain="Index Constituents",
    index="Dow Jones Industrial Average",
)

prices_daily = tf.download_data(
    domain="Stock Prices",
    symbols=symbols["symbol"].to_list(),
    start_date=start_date,
    end_date=end_date,
)
```
:::

## From daily prices to monthly returns

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: compute-monthly-returns-r
returns_monthly <- prices_daily |>
  arrange(symbol, date) |>
  mutate(date = floor_date(date, "month")) |>
  summarize(price = last(adjusted_close), .by = c(symbol, date)) |>
  mutate(ret = price / lag(price) - 1, .by = symbol) |>
  drop_na(ret) |>
  mutate(months = n(), .by = symbol) |>
  filter(months == max(months)) |>
  select(symbol, date, ret)
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: compute-monthly-returns-py
#| eval: false
returns_monthly = (
    prices_daily.sort("symbol", "date")
    .with_columns(date=pl.col("date").dt.truncate("1mo"))
    .group_by("symbol", "date", maintain_order=True)
    .agg(price=pl.col("adjusted_close").last())
    .with_columns(ret=pl.col("price").pct_change().over("symbol"))
    .drop_nulls("ret")
    .with_columns(months=pl.len().over("symbol"))
    .filter(pl.col("months") == pl.col("months").max())
    .select("symbol", "date", "ret")
)
```
:::

```{r}
#| label: sample-size
#| include: false
n_stocks <- n_distinct(returns_monthly$symbol)
n_months <- n_distinct(returns_monthly$date)
first_month <- format(min(returns_monthly$date), "%B %Y")
last_month <- format(max(returns_monthly$date), "%B %Y")
```

`r n_stocks` of today's 30 stocks have a return in every month from `r first_month` to `r last_month`: `r n_months` months. The same data as in the Tidy Finance chapter [Modern portfolio theory](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/modern-portfolio-theory.html) and in exercise 2

## Returns and portfolios

- $N$ assets with returns $r_t$ ($N \times 1$), expected returns $\mu = E(r_t)$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma = \text{Cov}(r_t)$
- A portfolio $\omega$ ($N \times 1$) invests all wealth: $\iota'\omega = 1$, with $\iota$ a vector of ones
- Its return is $r_{p,t} = \omega' r_t$, with

$$
E(r_{p,t}) = \omega'\mu \qquad \text{Var}(r_{p,t}) = \omega'\Sigma\omega
$$

- In practice, we replace $\mu$ and $\Sigma$ with their sample estimates

$$
\hat\mu = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T r_t \qquad \hat\Sigma = \frac{1}{T-1}\sum_{t=1}^T (r_t - \hat\mu)(r_t - \hat\mu)'
$$

## Expected returns and the covariance matrix

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: estimate-moments-r
returns_matrix <- returns_monthly |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = symbol, values_from = ret) |>
  select(-date) |>
  as.matrix()

mu <- colMeans(returns_matrix)
sigma <- cov(returns_matrix)
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: estimate-moments-py
#| eval: false
returns_matrix = (
    returns_monthly.pivot(on="symbol", index="date", values="ret")
    .drop("date")
    .to_numpy()
)

mu = returns_matrix.mean(axis=0)
sigma = np.cov(returns_matrix, rowvar=False)
```
:::

## `r n_stocks` stocks, one risk-return trade-off?

```{r}
#| label: plot-risk-return
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.2
assets <- tibble(
  symbol = colnames(returns_matrix),
  mu = mu * months_per_year,
  sigma = sqrt(diag(sigma) * months_per_year)
)

ggplot(assets, aes(x = sigma, y = mu, label = symbol)) +
  geom_point(color = jet) +
  geom_text_repel(size = 3.6, color = grey, seed = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(
    x = "Volatility (annualized)", y = "Expected return (annualized)",
    title = paste0("Dow Jones stocks, monthly returns ", first_month, " to ", last_month)
  )
```

## Diversification

```{r}
#| label: plot-diversification
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.4
# Variance of an equal-weighted portfolio of n stocks with average variance
# and average covariance: (1 / n) * variance + (1 - 1 / n) * covariance
average_variance <- mean(diag(sigma))
average_covariance <- mean(sigma[upper.tri(sigma)])

diversification <- tibble(n = 1:n_stocks) |>
  mutate(
    volatility = sqrt(
      (average_variance / n + (1 - 1 / n) * average_covariance) * months_per_year
    )
  )
volatility_floor <- sqrt(average_covariance * months_per_year)

ggplot(diversification, aes(x = n, y = volatility)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = volatility_floor, color = ku_red, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate(
    "text", x = n_stocks, y = volatility_floor, vjust = 1.8, hjust = 1, color = ku_red,
    label = "Risk that diversification cannot remove: the average covariance"
  ) +
  geom_line(color = jet, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(color = jet) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of stocks in an equal-weighted portfolio", y = "Volatility (annualized)",
    title = "Diversification: the volatility of an average equal-weighted portfolio"
  )
```

One stock: `r percent(sqrt(average_variance * months_per_year), 0.1)` volatility on average; `r n_stocks` stocks: `r percent(last(diversification$volatility), 0.1)`. Variances diversify away, covariances do not

# Mean-variance optimization

## Mean-variance preferences

- Investors like expected return and dislike variance (Markowitz, 1952)
- With risk aversion $\gamma$, the certainty equivalent of a portfolio is

$$
\text{CE}(\omega) = \omega'\mu - \frac{\gamma}{2}\,\omega'\Sigma\omega
$$

- Exact for quadratic utility or normally distributed returns, an approximation otherwise
- Equivalent problem: the lowest variance for a given expected return. Exercise 2 asks you to show it

::: {.highlight}
**The question of today:** which portfolios should a mean-variance investor hold?
:::

## Whiteboard: the minimum-variance portfolio

::: {.box}
$$
\omega_\text{mvp} = \arg\min_\omega \ \omega'\Sigma\omega \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \iota'\omega = 1
$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
\omega_\text{mvp} = \frac{\Sigma^{-1}\iota}{\iota'\Sigma^{-1}\iota} \qquad \text{Var}(r_\text{mvp}) = \frac{1}{\iota'\Sigma^{-1}\iota}
$$

- It needs only $\Sigma$, no expected returns
:::

Written out: Tidy Finance, [Proofs: minimum variance portfolio](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/proofs.html#minimum-variance-portfolio)

## The minimum-variance portfolio of the Dow Jones 30

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: compute-mvp-r
iota <- rep(1, ncol(sigma))
sigma_inv <- solve(sigma)

omega_mvp <- as.vector(sigma_inv %*% iota) / sum(sigma_inv %*% iota)
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: compute-mvp-py
#| eval: false
iota = np.ones(len(mu))
sigma_inv = np.linalg.inv(sigma)

omega_mvp = sigma_inv @ iota / (iota @ sigma_inv @ iota)
```
:::

```{r}
#| label: plot-mvp-weights
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8
mvp_mu <- sum(omega_mvp * mu) * months_per_year
mvp_sigma <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(omega_mvp) %*% sigma %*% omega_mvp) * months_per_year)

tibble(symbol = colnames(returns_matrix), weight = omega_mvp) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(symbol, weight), y = weight, fill = weight > 0)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = ku_red, `FALSE` = grey), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Weight",
    title = paste0(
      "Minimum-variance weights: expected return ", percent(mvp_mu, 0.1),
      ", volatility ", percent(mvp_sigma, 0.1), " (annualized)"
    )
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))
```

## Whiteboard: the efficient portfolio

::: {.box}
$$
\omega_\text{eff}(\bar\mu) = \arg\min_\omega \ \omega'\Sigma\omega \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \iota'\omega = 1, \ \ \omega'\mu = \bar\mu
$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
With $C = \iota'\Sigma^{-1}\iota$, $D = \iota'\Sigma^{-1}\mu$ and $E = \mu'\Sigma^{-1}\mu$:

$$
\omega_\text{eff}(\bar\mu) = \omega_\text{mvp} + \frac{\bar\mu - D/C}{E - D^2/C}\left(\Sigma^{-1}\mu - \frac{D}{C}\Sigma^{-1}\iota\right)
$$

- **Two-fund separation:** every efficient portfolio is a combination of two efficient portfolios, e.g. $a\,\omega_\text{eff}(\bar\mu) + (1 - a)\,\omega_\text{mvp}$
:::

Written out: Tidy Finance, [Proofs: efficient portfolio](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/proofs.html#efficient-portfolio)

## The efficient frontier of the Dow Jones 30

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: compute-efficient-frontier-r
C <- as.numeric(t(iota) %*% sigma_inv %*% iota)
D <- as.numeric(t(iota) %*% sigma_inv %*% mu)
E <- as.numeric(t(mu) %*% sigma_inv %*% mu)

# An efficient portfolio with three times the expected return of the mvp
mu_bar <- 3 * sum(omega_mvp * mu)
omega_eff <- omega_mvp + (mu_bar - D / C) / (E - D^2 / C) *
  as.vector(sigma_inv %*% mu - D / C * sigma_inv %*% iota)

efficient_frontier <- tibble(a = seq(-0.4, 1.9, by = 0.01)) |>
  mutate(
    omega = map(a, \(a) a * omega_eff + (1 - a) * omega_mvp),
    mu = map_dbl(omega, \(omega) sum(omega * mu)),
    sigma = map_dbl(omega, \(omega) sqrt(t(omega) %*% sigma %*% omega))
  )
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: compute-efficient-frontier-py
#| eval: false
C = iota @ sigma_inv @ iota
D = iota @ sigma_inv @ mu
E = mu @ sigma_inv @ mu

# An efficient portfolio with three times the expected return of the mvp
mu_bar = 3 * omega_mvp @ mu
omega_eff = omega_mvp + (mu_bar - D / C) / (E - D**2 / C) * (
    sigma_inv @ mu - D / C * sigma_inv @ iota
)

a_grid = np.arange(-0.4, 1.91, 0.01)
omegas = [a * omega_eff + (1 - a) * omega_mvp for a in a_grid]
efficient_frontier = pl.DataFrame({
    "a": a_grid,
    "mu": [omega @ mu for omega in omegas],
    "sigma": [np.sqrt(omega @ sigma @ omega) for omega in omegas],
})
```
:::

## The efficient frontier

```{r}
#| label: plot-efficient-frontier
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.2
frontier_annual <- efficient_frontier |>
  mutate(mu = mu * months_per_year, sigma = sigma * sqrt(months_per_year))
mvp_point <- tibble(symbol = "Minimum variance", mu = mvp_mu, sigma = mvp_sigma)

ggplot(mapping = aes(x = sigma, y = mu)) +
  geom_path(data = frontier_annual, color = jet, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = assets, color = grey) +
  geom_text_repel(data = assets, aes(label = symbol), size = 3.2, color = grey, seed = 1) +
  geom_point(data = mvp_point, color = ku_red, size = 3) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = mvp_point, aes(label = symbol), color = ku_red, nudge_x = -0.06, seed = 1
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(
    x = "Volatility (annualized)", y = "Expected return (annualized)",
    title = "The efficient frontier of the Dow Jones stocks"
  )
```

# Adding a risk-free asset

## Whiteboard: the tangency portfolio

- Invest $\omega$ in the risky assets and $1 - \iota'\omega$ at the risk-free rate $r_f$: expected return $r_f + \omega'(\mu - r_f\iota)$, variance $\omega'\Sigma\omega$

::: {.box}
$$
\min_\omega \ \omega'\Sigma\omega \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \omega'(\mu - r_f\iota) = \bar\mu - r_f
$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
- The solution is proportional to $\Sigma^{-1}(\mu - r_f\iota)$. All risky wealth goes into the **tangency portfolio**

$$
\omega_\text{tan} = \frac{\Sigma^{-1}(\mu - r_f\iota)}{\iota'\Sigma^{-1}(\mu - r_f\iota)}
$$

- It has the highest Sharpe ratio $(\mu_\text{tan} - r_f)/\sigma_\text{tan}$ of all portfolios, the slope of the **capital market line** through $r_f$
:::

## The tangency portfolio of the Dow Jones 30

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: compute-tangency-r
# The average one-month T-bill rate over the sample
rf <- read_parquet("data/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet") |>
  filter(date >= start_date, date <= end_date) |>
  summarize(rf = mean(risk_free)) |>
  pull(rf)

omega_tan <- as.vector(sigma_inv %*% (mu - rf))
omega_tan <- omega_tan / sum(omega_tan)
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: compute-tangency-py
#| eval: false
# The average one-month T-bill rate over the sample
rf = (
    pl.read_parquet("data/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet")
    .filter(
        pl.col("date") >= pl.lit(start_date).str.to_date(),
        pl.col("date") <= pl.lit(end_date).str.to_date(),
    )
    .get_column("risk_free")
    .mean()
)

omega_tan = sigma_inv @ (mu - rf)
omega_tan = omega_tan / omega_tan.sum()
```
:::

```{r}
#| label: tangency-summary
#| include: false
tan_mu <- sum(omega_tan * mu) * months_per_year
tan_sigma <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(omega_tan) %*% sigma %*% omega_tan) * months_per_year)
tan_sharpe <- (tan_mu - rf * months_per_year) / tan_sigma
rf_annual <- rf * months_per_year
```

The average T-bill rate is `r percent(rf_annual, 0.1)` a year. The tangency portfolio has an expected return of `r percent(tan_mu, 0.1)` at a volatility of `r percent(tan_sigma, 0.1)`: a Sharpe ratio of `r number(tan_sharpe, 0.01)` (annualized)

## The capital market line

```{r}
#| label: plot-capital-market-line
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.2
tangency_point <- tibble(label = "Tangency", mu = tan_mu, sigma = tan_sigma)

ggplot(mapping = aes(x = sigma, y = mu)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = rf_annual, slope = tan_sharpe, color = ku_red, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_path(data = frontier_annual, color = jet, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = assets, color = grey) +
  geom_point(data = tangency_point, color = ku_red, size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = 0, y = rf_annual), color = ku_red, size = 2) +
  geom_label_repel(data = tangency_point, aes(label = label), color = ku_red, nudge_x = -0.08, seed = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(
    x = "Volatility (annualized)", y = "Expected return (annualized)",
    title = paste0("Frontier with a risk-free rate of ", percent(rf_annual, 0.1), ": the capital market line")
  )
```

## Which point on the line?

- An investor with risk aversion $\gamma$ maximizes the certainty equivalent with a risk-free asset:

$$
\omega^* = \frac{1}{\gamma}\,\Sigma^{-1}(\mu - r_f\iota)
$$

- $\omega^*$ is proportional to $\omega_\text{tan}$: every mean-variance investor holds the **same risky portfolio**, mixed with the risk-free asset
- Risk aversion only decides the mix: the share in risky assets is $\iota'\omega^*$, the rest is borrowed or lent at $r_f$

::: {.highlight}
**Two-fund separation (Tobin, 1958):** the tangency portfolio and the risk-free asset are all an investor needs
:::

## The risk-free rate moves the tangency portfolio

```{r}
#| label: slider-inputs
#| include: false
# The slider needs only a few vectors: the tangency weights for a monthly
# risk-free rate r are (a - r b) / (D - r C)
slider_a <- as.vector(sigma_inv %*% mu)
slider_b <- as.vector(sigma_inv %*% iota)

if (live) {
  ojs_define(
    poll_base = poll_base,
    allocation_poll = allocation_poll,
    allocation_choices = allocation_choices,
    stocks = assets,
    frontier = frontier_annual |> select(mu, sigma),
    weights_inputs = tibble(symbol = colnames(returns_matrix), a = slider_a, b = slider_b),
    moments = list(C = C, D = D, E = E, months = months_per_year)
  )
}
```

//| label: risk-free-slider
//| echo: false
viewof rf_annual = Inputs.range([0, 14], {step: 0.25, value: 2, width: 520, label: "Risk-free rate, % per year"})

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
```{ojs}
//| label: tangency-frontier-live
//| echo: false
r = rf_annual / 100 / moments.months
denominator = moments.D - r * moments.C
tangency = ({
  mu: (moments.E - r * moments.D) / denominator * moments.months,
  sigma: Math.sqrt(moments.E - 2 * r * moments.D + r * r * moments.C) / Math.abs(denominator) * Math.sqrt(moments.months)
})
slope = (tangency.mu - rf_annual / 100) / tangency.sigma
sigma_max = 0.6
Plot.plot({
  width: 620,
  height: 420,
  x: {label: "Volatility (annualized)", domain: [0, sigma_max], tickFormat: "%"},
  y: {label: "Expected return (annualized)", domain: [-0.1, 0.6], tickFormat: "%"},
  marks: [
    Plot.line(transpose(frontier), {x: "sigma", y: "mu", stroke: "#3d3d3d", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.dot(transpose(stocks), {x: "sigma", y: "mu", fill: "#666666", r: 3}),
    Plot.line([{sigma: 0, mu: rf_annual / 100}, {sigma: sigma_max, mu: rf_annual / 100 + slope * sigma_max}],
              {x: "sigma", y: "mu", stroke: "#901A1E", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.dot([{sigma: 0, mu: rf_annual / 100}], {x: "sigma", y: "mu", fill: "#901A1E", r: 5}),
    Plot.dot([tangency], {x: "sigma", y: "mu", fill: "#901A1E", r: 7}),
    Plot.text([tangency], {x: "sigma", y: "mu", text: d => "Tangency", dy: -14, fill: "#901A1E"})
  ]
})
```

::: {.content-visible unless-profile="live"}
```{r}
#| label: plot-tangency-by-risk-free-rate
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.2
tangency_by_rate <- tibble(rf_annual = risk_free_rates_shown) |>
  mutate(
    omega = map(rf_annual, \(rate) {
      omega <- as.vector(sigma_inv %*% (mu - rate / months_per_year))
      omega / sum(omega)
    }),
    mu = map_dbl(omega, \(omega) sum(omega * mu) * months_per_year),
    sigma = map_dbl(omega, \(omega) sqrt(t(omega) %*% sigma %*% omega * months_per_year)),
    slope = (mu - rf_annual) / sigma,
    rate = fct_inorder(paste0(percent(rf_annual), " risk-free rate"))
  )
rate_colors <- set_names(c("#b3b3b3", jet, ku_red), levels(tangency_by_rate$rate))

frontier_panel <- ggplot(mapping = aes(x = sigma, y = mu)) +
  geom_abline(
    data = tangency_by_rate, aes(intercept = rf_annual, slope = slope, color = rate),
    linewidth = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_path(data = frontier_annual, color = jet, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = assets, color = grey, size = 1) +
  geom_point(data = tangency_by_rate, aes(color = rate), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = rate_colors) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 0.6), ylim = c(-0.05, 0.6)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(x = "Volatility (annualized)", y = "Expected return (annualized)", color = NULL)

weights_panel <- tangency_by_rate |>
  mutate(omega = map(omega, \(omega) tibble(symbol = colnames(returns_matrix), weight = omega))) |>
  select(rate, omega) |>
  unnest(omega) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = weight, y = fct_reorder(symbol, weight), color = rate)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = light) +
  geom_line(aes(group = symbol), color = light) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = rate_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(x = "Tangency weight", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9))

frontier_panel + weights_panel + plot_layout(widths = c(1.4, 1), guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
:::

# What could go wrong?

## Would you hold this portfolio?

```{r}
#| label: tangency-extremes
#| include: false
n_short <- sum(omega_tan < 0)
largest_weight <- max(omega_tan)
largest_stock <- colnames(returns_matrix)[which.max(omega_tan)]
```

- The tangency portfolio promises `r percent(tan_mu, 0.1)` a year at `r percent(tan_sigma, 0.1)` volatility, more than any single stock offers at that risk
- It shorts `r n_short` of the `r n_stocks` stocks; its largest position is `r percent(largest_weight, 0.1)` in `r largest_stock`
- Compare it with how you split your \$1

::: {.highlight}
Every number rests on $\hat\mu$ and $\hat\Sigma$, estimated from the same `r n_months` months. How much of it survives out of sample? Next lecture: **estimation uncertainty**
:::
